NLF Chapter 10? Chef’s kiss.

Thousands of young minds and parents spent the day meeting authors, making friends, getting inspired and discovering a little more about themselves along the way.

And just like that, it’s time to say goodbye.

Until then, read, write and keep telling stories from the heart.

And that was just Day 1!

The only weekend where kids and adults looked forward to a 10 AM session, and even wished it started earlier!

From inspiring masterclasses and hands-on workshops to author autographs worth holding on to, Day 1 had something for every curious mind.

And the best part? Day Two awaits.

We’re excited to welcome bestselling author Amish Tripathi to NLF! 

Known for the Shiva Trilogy and Ram Chandra Series, Amish is now bringing his storytelling to young readers with Dhruv-Tara & The Great Indian History Quiz, the first book in a planned seven-book series.

Straight from our young readers, this year’s Student’s Choice Award goes to The White Lotus by Aditi Krishnakumar, published by Duckbill, an imprint of Penguin Random House India.

Set in rural Tamil Nadu in 1901, The White Lotus follows fourteen-year-old Aru, who is widowed just as her life is beginning. When an unexpected opportunity takes her to a landlord’s household, she finds a chance at education and a life beyond the confines of widowhood. But when uncomfortable truths begin to surface and her life is put in danger, Aru finds herself at the centre of a gripping mystery. With its compelling characters, rich historical setting and powerful portrait of resilience and hope, The White Lotus is a story that stays with you long after the final page.

We’re delighted to announce that this year’s Neev Book Award for distinguished children’s literature goes to HJBRL, based on the novella by Sukumar Ray, brilliantly reimagined as a graphic novel by Charbak Dipta and published by HarperCollins India.

A timeless work of nonsense literature, HJBRL takes readers into a wonderfully absurd world where handkerchiefs become cats, crows do accounting, and characters appear and disappear with the most unexpected explanations. With its vibrant artwork and playful visual storytelling, Charbak Dipta brings Sukumar Ray’s iconic imagination to a new generation of readers. A celebration of the wonderfully weird, HJBRL reminds us that children’s literature can delight, surprise and make us see the world a little differently.

Our biggest chapter yet, now all yours! 

PS: Post about your experience and don’t forget to tag us. We can’t wait to see it through your eyes.

Now that’s a shoutout from the heart ❤️

Thank you so much, paroanand. We’ll dearly miss your love and warmth at NLF this year 🙁
